evidence.claim: Onto Innovation's annual report describes advanced-node metrology down to 7nm, 5nm, and 3nm and discusses advanced packaging, 3D integration, and AI-driven demand creating new technology requirements.

Onto's 2025 fourth-quarter/full-year results release states that global AI investment is fueling demand and that its position in advanced packaging, advanced nodes, and specialty devices supports growth-segment exposure.
evidence.source_title: Onto Innovation Reports 2025 Fourth Quarter and Full-Year Results

evidence.claim: Camtek states that its systems serve demanding semiconductor segments including advanced interconnect packaging, heterogeneous integration, memory, and HBM, and that it has seen increased demand from AI-related products including HBM and advanced packaging.
Camtek's investor page describes its systems as inspecting and measuring wafers through front-end, mid-end, and early assembly processes for global IDMs, OSATs, and foundries.

Entegris describes itself as a supplier of critical advanced materials and process solutions, including filtration, purification, contamination control, advanced deposition materials, selective etch formulations, EUV reticle pods, and wafer carriers for advanced nodes.

Because leading-edge logic and EUV processes are highly sensitive to defects, Entegris' filtration, purification, and advanced materials portfolio may be an underappreciated yield-enabling exposure to AI chip capacity ramps.

MKS's 2025 annual report materials state that its semiconductor business benefited from higher demand for critical subsystems used in deposition and etch and that electronics/packaging benefited from AI server complexity.
MKS may benefit as a second-order supplier to primary wafer-fab equipment vendors if AI-driven leading-edge capex increases demand for deposition, etch, process-control, and packaging subsystems.

Amkor's 2025 10-K says it provides packaging and test services after wafer fabrication and defines Advanced Products as flip chip, memory, wafer-level processing, and related test services; Apple and Qualcomm were major customers in 2025.
Apple announced that it is investing in Amkor's new advanced chip packaging and test facility in Arizona and expects to be its first and largest customer.
evidence.source_title: Apple increases U.S. commitment to $600 billion, announces ambitious program

evidence.claim: TSMC's 2025 annual report says AI market developments remained very positive and highlights advanced process technologies plus advanced packaging and 3D chip-stacking solutions including CoWoS, InFO, SoIC, and COUPE.
ASML's 2025 annual report discusses portfolio-wide innovation for complex semiconductor manufacturing and lists AI and advanced packaging among monitored opportunities and demand drivers.

memory_update.text: ONTO added as a focused metrology/inspection candidate for advanced packaging, HBM, hybrid bonding, and advanced-node process control linked to AI chip manufacturing.
CAMT added as a focused inspection/metrology candidate with explicit AI, HBM, and advanced-packaging demand exposure; validate customer concentration and platform adoption.
ENTG added as an underappreciated materials/purity/yield-enabler for advanced nodes, EUV, selective etch, deposition materials, CMP, filtration, and contamination control.
MKSI added as a second-order semiconductor equipment subsystem supplier with exposure to deposition/etch, process control, vacuum, and electronics/advanced packaging demand.
AMKR added as an adjacent advanced packaging/test capacity candidate, especially for U.S.-based packaging linked to TSMC Arizona and Apple supply-chain commitments.

For this node, the less-obvious chokepoint map should include not only foundries and primary WFE vendors, but also advanced packaging/test, metrology/inspection, high-purity materials, and WFE subsystem suppliers.
Still need a separate pass on EDA/IP and test vendors such as Synopsys, Cadence, Arm, Teradyne, and Advantest, plus specialized gases/chemicals where US-listed exposure may be indirect.

node: Leading-edge foundry capacity and semiconductor equipment
summary: Expanded the universe for the leading-edge foundry/equipment node toward less-obvious second-order beneficiaries: advanced packaging/test capacity, metrology/inspection for HBM and chiplets, contamination-control materials, and critical subsystems used inside deposition/etch/lithography equipment. These are not recommendations; they are research candidates whose AI exposure should be verified through revenue mix, backlog, customer concentration, shipment timing, China/export-control exposure, and capex-cycle sensitivity.
